_comment: dataset_name  Folder name under datasets/generated/ that output is
written into, e.g. datasets/generated/base/.
sample_defaults  Global scans/duration_hrs/duration_mins target for
the --samples tier (see generate_synthetic_data.py),
applied to every experiment unless overridden by that
experiment's own 'samples' object below. Must never be
more than what an experiment's own simparams.xml
specifies, and must never reduce scans to 0 or duration
to 0 -- the generator asserts both at build time.
experiments is a flat list. One physical rotor/run per experiment;
one or more channels per experiment (one physical channel each).
Experiment-level fields (shared across all of an experiment's channels):
id            Unique identifier for the experiment, used as the zip
basename and as the key the generator looks entries up
by internally, e.g. 'netrin1-ra'.
dir           The output directory this experiment's zip is written
to: datasets/generated/base/<dir>/ by default, or
datasets/generated/base/samples/<dir>/ with --samples.
Directory name only -- not used as a lookup key.
simparams     dir under config/simparams/ holding this experiment's
base simparams.xml (speed, duration, scan count, point
count, noise, etc.), used exactly as checked in unless
--samples is passed. Multiple experiments may share one.
rotor         Rotor definition ID passed to us_astfem_sim/
us_mwl_species_sim --rotor, e.g. '1'. Unrelated to any
rotor calibration inside simparams.xml.
description   Human-readable note for the generated README's Summary
table. The generator appends the live-computed s value
itself -- don't put s here.
samples       Optional. Per-experiment override of sample_defaults --
any of scans/duration_hrs/duration_mins, merged over
the global defaults key-by-key. Same never-more-than-
original/never-zero rule applies.
Per-channel fields (inside the channels list):
channel       Naming label only, e.g. '1A' -- no physics meaning,
used for mwl model filenames.
model         dir under config/models/ -- independent of buffer.
buffer        dir under config/buffers/ -- independent of model.
data_type     The 2-byte .auc data type this channel is relabeled
to (RA=Absorbance, RI=Interference, IP=Intensity,
FI=Fluorescence, WI=Wavelength), or e.g. 'RI/IP' for a
channel whose single run is duplicated and tagged both
ways.
centerpiece   Optional. Which centerpiece type (effectively which
cell) -- index into etc/abstractCenterpieces.xml.
Omit to inherit 0. Channels sharing a cell use the
same value.
centerpiece_channel  Optional. Which radial row/pair within that
centerpiece a channel belongs to (0, 1, ... -- resets
per centerpiece, not global across cells). Omit to
inherit 0. A row is one radial level shared by BOTH
sectors of a sample/reference pair (side-by-side
angularly, identical bottom/pathlen) -- so channels
sharing one cell/pair use the SAME value here, not
different ones. Only give channels different values
when they occupy different radial rows of the same
multi-row (e.g. 6- or 8-sector equilibrium)
centerpiece.
wavelengths   Optional, comma-separated nm values, e.g. 250,280,310.
Only present on multi-wavelength channels -- its
presence is what marks a channel as mwl.
mwl_run_id    Optional, only alongside wavelengths. Short label used
to name this channel's generated per-wavelength model
files, e.g. 'synth-mwl-001'.
rnoise/lrnoise/tinoise/rinoise/baseline  Optional. Per-channel output
variation -- safe to override (doesn't feed
calc_bottom()), unlike centerpiece/centerpiece_channel.
Omit to inherit the experiment's base simparams.xml
values. Use to make channels not look identical, e.g.
a noisier reference channel.
signal        Optional. Per-channel signal_concentration (the
OD-clamp ceiling in save_xla()) -- also safe to
override, patched into model.xml instead of
simparams.xml. Omit to inherit 1.0 (every checked-in
model.xml's default, and the only value
us_sim_inputs_gen --emit-model ever
write). Use to make one channel/experiment's magnitude
distinct from another's instead of every dataset
sharing the same fixed ceiling regardless of its real
sedimentation coefficient.
Multiple experiments may share buffers/models, e.g. the two
dna-monomer-208bp channels below are the same DNA prep in the same
buffer, just tagged/packaged differently.
